category_title: Students who use defensive social put-downs when challenged
minimal_context: The student is participating in a small-group discussion to predict which cup of water will make an egg float and explain the mass differences between the cups.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We have two cups of water and an egg. Which cup do you predict will make the egg float?

STUDENT: I think that this one because of the salt water, it will hold the egg up.

TUTOR: Let's look at the cups on the scale. What do you observe?

STUDENT: This has two things: salt and water. And that one has just one thing.

TUTOR: Notice that both cups have equal volume, but different weights. Why do you think that is?

STUDENT: That’s because it has an extra thing. It makes it heavier.

options.A: Walk around the room and stand directly behind the student during the small-group discussion.
options.B: Give a scenario about a store where they wanted to buy salt but did not know the word 'salt'.
options.C: Quickly devise a supplementary hands-on activity to review the missing concept (e.g., mass) during the discussion.
options.D: Control the process, rather than the content, of the small-group discussion about the cups.
